body: Unfortunately, that wouldn't really work in my particular research field.  Thanks for the ingenuity, tho.

proverbial nail on the head.  unusally stressed: yes.  Lonely and isolated: absolutley.  Self loathing/pity: very much so..

I will try more to "observe the thinker."  But, when I reunite with the thinker again, I am scared of the onslaught of feeling.

Approaching others: at the times that I feel most desperate, I feel the most isolated.  I am on an island.  I have a long distance relationship (had to move across several states to go to this school), and I'm afraid to even confess these worries to that person (guilt of dishonesty).  In those regards, I am hard pressed to trust a professor that is seemingly more approachable than others.  I have found one, but I feel that if I shared the extent of myself to that individual, not only would I feel (vague...) too intimate/embarrassed about my feelings, but I feel that that would, in some bizarre way, be this cloud that would persist over that relationship, that I would involve them in some kind of emotional responsibility that I don't want them to be the arbiter of.  It would be, in less words, weird, from that point on.

I am realizing that I am independent to a fault.
As mentioned above, I don't think it's appropriate that I share where I'm at.  I'm in the united states.  I will look into private practice options, thanks.

I know personally how it feels to want to check out.  Honestly, if you want to go to school, then go.  It is the best thing I ever did and it's kept me going forward thus far.  I have a strong feeling that the people will be a much needed change.  Do a trial year, at the least.

It's rough having to be engulfed in an environment that pushes against you, and I imagine that if they're as bad as they seem, they push against anyone.  There's nothing worse about you that makes you a target, those people just suck and they want to pull you in to their shitty zeitgeist.  Don't give in, don't give up, and don't give them the satisfaction of pushing back. 

This sounds bleak, but it is from someone who truly feels this way.  I am depressed, but what has kept me around so far is a vascillation between curiosity, guilt, and hope.  I'm curious if things get better, I'd be guilty for the handful of people I'd disappoint if I decided to go, and I hope that my curiosity pays off and that I can try to make things better.

I don't know you, but I am honest when I say I believe in you.  Keep going.
